passage:
I'll tell you what worked. I suspected my sister Himani had lost her job weeks ago, because she kept leaving in the morning and coming back too early. I'm Rukmini, and my first thought was to accuse her. Instead, one Sunday over tea, I said, "Himani, I've been wondering about work. I would prefer the truth to being shielded from it. And I promise I won't explode or lecture."
She looked at her cup for a long time. Then she said, "I lost the job in March. I didn't want you to worry." I said, "Thank you for telling me." We sat there and she cried, and I made more tea.

qa.q: When did Himani say she lost the job?
qa.a: Himani said she lost the job in March.

qa.q: What was Rukmini feeling and wanting before the Sunday tea?
qa.a: Rukmini was worried and suspicious but wanted the truth without a fight. Choosing not to accuse shows a wish to make honesty safe.

qa.q: What did Rukmini say that made honesty easier?
qa.a: Rukmini said she would prefer the truth to being shielded from it and promised not to explode or lecture. That lowered the cost of telling the truth.

qa.q: How might Himani have felt when Rukmini said "I won't explode or lecture"?
qa.a: Himani probably felt both nervous and relieved, since she stared at her cup and then told the truth. The promise made it safer to say it.

grounding: A person who suspects a lie says they prefer the truth to being shielded from it, and promises not to explode; honesty follows.

I sat two desks from Manjula, so I heard the whole exchange in the pantry. Yash had been avoiding her for days, and she seemed to know something was off. She stopped him gently by the tea machine.
"Yash, did the client actually cancel, or is there something more? I want the real story, not a shielded one. I won't blow up, I promise."
Yash looked at his shoes. "They cancelled Friday. I didn't know how to tell you."
Manjula nodded. "Thank you for saying it. Let's work out what to do."
I couldn't tell you what she felt inside. But her hands were steady, and Yash's shoulders came down.
— Tarun

qa.q: Where did Manjula speak to Yash?
qa.a: Manjula spoke to Yash by the tea machine in the pantry.

qa.q: What might Yash have been feeling when looking at his shoes?
qa.a: Yash was probably uneasy and ashamed, having avoided Manjula for days. Tarun can only guess from what showed.

qa.q: What did Manjula say that made honesty possible?
qa.a: Manjula said she wanted the real story, not a shielded one, and promised not to blow up. Then she thanked Yash and moved to a plan.

qa.q: How might it have looked to Tarun that Manjula stayed calm?
qa.a: Tarun saw steady hands and a calm voice and could not say what she felt inside. The calm made it easy for Yash to speak.

grounding: A person who suspects a lie asks for the real story, promises not to blow up, and gets an honest answer, as seen by someone at work.

passage:
Day one. Ankita, twenty-five, noticed her younger sister Avni was home at noon on a weekday, again. "No classes?" "Cancelled." It was the third time that week.
Day four. Avni's college sent a message to the family email: attendance below requirement. Ankita's first urge was to march in and say, "So you've been lying to all of us?"
She didn't. She waited until evening and sat on Avni's bed. "Avni, I got an email from college. I'm not going to explode. I'd much rather hear the real story from you than be shielded from it. Whatever it is, we'll figure it out."
Avni's face crumpled. "I hate the course. I've been sitting in the library, not going to class. I didn't know how to tell Papa."
Day ten. The sisters sat with Papa together. Avni did the talking. Ankita held her hand.

qa.q: What did the college email say?
qa.a: It said attendance was below requirement.

qa.q: What was Ankita feeling when the email arrived?
qa.a: Ankita felt angry and betrayed, wanting to march in and accuse Avni of lying to them all.

qa.q: What made it easier for Avni to tell the truth?
qa.a: Ankita promised not to explode, said she'd rather hear the real story, and offered to solve it together, which lowered the cost of honesty.

qa.q: Why had Avni been hiding the truth?
qa.a: Avni felt trapped and afraid, hating the course but not knowing how to tell Papa.

grounding: A person who suspects a lie says she would rather hear the truth and won't explode, making honesty safer than accusation.

passage:
"Kunal, you're a manager now, so let your Sangeeta ma'am tell you something she learnt the hard way.
"My first year leading a team, a junior called Ravi said a report had been sent to the client. I found out the next day it hadn't. Then another thing. And another. I called him into my cabin and said, 'You've been lying to me.' He went pale and said nothing. Next week, he lied again.
"My old boss told me: 'Accusations make people hide better.'
"So the next time, I called Ravi for tea. I said, 'Ravi, I'd rather know when something is late than be protected from it. I promise I won't blow up. Is anything stuck?'
"He told me everything. His mother was unwell, and he was drowning in work.
"We shared out his load for a month. He never lied to me again.
"Make the truth cheap, Kunal. It's the only way you'll hear it.

qa.q: Who was the junior who kept lying?
qa.a: A junior called Ravi.

qa.q: How did Ravi feel when Sangeeta accused him of lying?
qa.a: Ravi went pale and silent, frightened and ashamed, and then kept hiding things.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Sangeeta's story, and why did it work?
qa.a: She invited Ravi for tea, promised not to blow up and asked if anything was stuck, which made telling the truth cheaper than hiding it.

qa.q: What had Ravi been hiding, and how did it feel for him?
qa.a: Ravi was hiding that his mother was unwell and he was drowning in work, which left him overwhelmed and afraid to admit it.

grounding: An elder recalls how accusations made a junior hide more, while inviting truth safely and promising calm brought honesty.

passage:
The power had gone out in their Lucknow flat, and Wasim and Ritu sat by a candle, waiting for the inverter to kick in. Ritu had been quiet all evening. Wasim had noticed the new scratch on the scooter and the fresh bandage on her elbow. She'd said she "bumped into a cupboard".
He felt the question rising, sharp: What really happened? Why are you lying? But he knew that tone would make her close up.
Instead he said, "Ritu, I noticed the scooter and your arm. I'd rather know than be protected. I promise I won't get angry. I just want to know you're okay."
She looked at the candle a long time. "I skidded near the market. I didn't want you to worry, or say I shouldn't ride."
"Are you hurt anywhere else?"
"Just my pride."
"Tomorrow, let's get the brakes checked. Together."

qa.q: What had Ritu said caused the bandage?
qa.a: She'd said she "bumped into a cupboard".

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling when he noticed the scratch and bandage?
qa.a: Wasim felt worried and a sharp frustration at the story, but held it back knowing anger would make Ritu close up.

qa.q: Which of Wasim's choices made honesty easier?
qa.a: He named what he noticed calmly, said he'd rather know than be protected and promised not to get angry, lowering the cost of the truth.

qa.q: Why had Ritu hidden the skid?
qa.a: Ritu felt embarrassed and afraid Wasim would worry or say she shouldn't ride.

grounding: A person who suspects a lie says he would rather know than be protected and won't get angry, and the truth comes out.

passage: Yusuf's scooter came back to the Jayanagar parking lot with a long scrape down the left side and the mirror twisted. Anjali handed over the keys without meeting his eyes. "It was like that when I took it, na?" Yusuf knew it wasn't; he had washed it on Sunday. He felt the heat rise and an accusation form. He swallowed it. "Anjali, sit for a sec." They sat on the low wall. "I'd honestly rather have it straight than be shielded from it. Whatever happened, I'm not going to blow up. It's a scooter." Anjali picked at her dupatta. A long pause. "I skidded on the gravel near the flyover. I was so embarrassed, and you'd just said how new it was." "Were you hurt?" "Just my palm." She showed it. "Okay. We'll get the mirror fixed Saturday." Anjali laughed shakily. "I'll pay for the mirror. And sorry."

qa.q: When had Yusuf washed the scooter?
qa.a: He had washed it on Sunday.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling when Anjali said it was like that before?
qa.a: Yusuf felt angry, the heat rising and an accusation forming, because he knew the scooter had been clean and whole.

qa.q: Which of Yusuf's choices made honesty easier?
qa.a: Swallowing the accusation, sitting down with Anjali, and saying he preferred the truth and would not blow up, which made confessing less costly.

qa.q: Why might Anjali have told the truth after Yusuf spoke?
qa.a: His promise not to blow up lowered the cost of honesty, so admitting her embarrassment felt safer than keeping up the story.

grounding: Shows a person who suspects a lie choosing to say he prefers the truth and will not explode, which makes an honest answer possible.
